rationale.conceptual: The method is a custom first-principles-derived approach combining effective Hamiltonian construction with local soft modes and strain, non-trivial MD in NPT and NVE ensembles, dipole autocorrelation using an overlap technique, and Fourier transform via fluctuation-dissipation; implementing this correctly demands genuine comprehension of ferroelectric physics and several interacting theoretical components.
rationale.execution: The pipeline involves multiple sequential stages: loading and implementing the effective Hamiltonian parameters, setting up a 14×14×14 supercell, performing lengthy NPT and NVE MD simulations (millions of timesteps), recording dipole trajectories, computing autocorrelation functions, numerical Fourier transforms, and fitting with two damped harmonic oscillators; orchestrating these stages with correct ensemble switching and data flow is substantial.

difficulty.reasoning: The paper develops a novel first-principles-based effective Hamiltonian molecular dynamics method to compute the terahertz dielectric response of BaTiO₃, requiring deep understanding of the model, fluctuation-dissipation theorem, and multi-stage simulation; it is a complex, multi-component pipeline with long MD production runs.

compute_estimate.reasoning: The effective-Hamiltonian model coarse-grains the system to soft-mode and strain variables, making MD tractable on a single CPU with modest memory (a few GB); no large external dataset is required, only the published Hamiltonian parameters.
